subtitle: Harsha’s great gift at the confluence of three rivers

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of the Sangam with a thronging multitude and Harsha at the center
panels.action: Harsha of Kannauj stands at the misty confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, bareheaded beneath a pale dawn, surrounded by piled treasures and a sea of monks, Brahmins, mendicants and nobles stretching to the horizon.

dialogue.text: At Prayag, once in five years, King Harsha turned a royal camp into a tide of gifts—where faiths met, fortunes shifted, and generosity itself became a weapon of rule.

i18n.hi: प्रयाग में हर पाँचवें साल हर्ष राजा का शाही डेरा दानों की लहर बन जाता है—जहाँ मज़हब टकराते हैं, किस्मतें बदलती हैं, और दान ही राज की हथियार बन जाता है।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of the Ganga-Yamuna confluence crowded with tents and processions
panels.action: From above, endless white tents and colorful pavilions line the sandy banks of the rivers, boats crowd the waters, and long processions wind towards a raised platform where Harsha’s royal canopy stands.

dialogue.text: It is around 642 CE. At the Sangam of Ganga and Yamuna, a city of cloth and rope rises for just a few days—the Moksha-Dana of King Harsha.

i18n.hi: लगभग ६४२ ई. का समय। गंगा–यमुना के संगम पर कुछ ही दिनों के लिए कपड़े और रस्सियों का शहर उठ खड़ा होता है—राजा हर्ष का मोक्ष-दान।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Harsha looking out over arriving delegations
panels.action: Seen from behind, Harsha stands in simple but fine robes, watching lines of arriving rulers, ascetics, merchants and villagers threading their way through dust and sun toward the central camp.

dialogue.text: Every five years he calls them here—vassal kings, monks and mendicants, Brahmins and Jains, traders and the poor—to witness a king unmake and remake his wealth.

i18n.hi: हर पाँच साल वह सबको बुलाता है—अधीन राजा, भिक्षु और साधु, ब्राह्मण और जैन, व्यापारी और ग़रीब—कि एक राजा को अपना धन तोड़ते और फिर से जोड़ते देख सकें।

panels.shot: close-up on Harsha’s thoughtful face lit by morning light
panels.action: A close view of Harsha’s face, eyes steady yet contemplative, as a cool river breeze lifts the edge of his turban and the distant sound of cymbals drifts across the sand.

dialogue.text: Xuanzang, the Chinese monk, will later write of this gathering. Through his eyes, we see not only piety, but a careful craft of power in every gesture.

i18n.hi: चीनी भिक्षु श्वेनज़ांग बाद में इस मेले का ब्योरा लिखेगा। उसकी आँखों से हम सिर्फ़ भक्ति नहीं, हर इशारे में बुनी सत्ता की चाल भी देखते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of three great enclosures around a central royal pavilion
panels.action: Three broad enclosures—one thronged with saffron-robed monks, another crowded with Brahmins in white and scholars with palm-leaf bundles, a third with Jains and other sects—stand facing a central royal pavilion where Harsha is seated.

dialogue.text: Here, the king orders the gathering by faith and station. Buddhists in one place, Brahmins in another, Jains and other ascetics in a third, with the hungry poor pressing at the edges.

i18n.hi: यहाँ राजा सबको मज़हब और पद के हिसाब से सजाता है। एक ओर बौद्ध, दूसरी ओर ब्राह्मण, तीसरी ओर जैन और तपस्वी, और किनारों पर भूखे ग़रीबों की भीड़।

panels.shot: medium wide of Harsha rising from his throne before an assembly of nobles
panels.action: Harsha rises from a low throne beneath his umbrella, flanked by subordinate kings and officials, while attendants hold trays piled with jewels, folded garments and golden vessels.

dialogue.text: To the courtly eye, this is not chaos. It is a ritual of redistribution: the king drains his treasury in public, while his lieutenants stand ready with their own gifts.

i18n.hi: दरबारी नज़र में यह अव्यवस्था नहीं। यह बाँटने की रस्म है: राजा सबके सामने कोश खाली करता है, और उसके सरदार अपने दान के साथ खड़े रहते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Harsha placing a jeweled crown on a monk’s hands as nobles watch
panels.action: Harsha leans forward, placing a heavy jeweled crown into the open hands of a serene Buddhist monk, while nearby Brahmins and nobles watch in a hush, animals and attendants waiting behind.

dialogue.text: He begins with monks, as Xuanzang records, granting rich gifts to the Buddhist community. But the line of receivers does not end with them.

i18n.hi: शुरुआत भिक्षुओं से होती है, जैसा श्वेनज़ांग लिखता है—बौद्ध संघ को भारी दान मिलता है। पर लेने वालों की क़तार वहीं नहीं रुकती।

panels.shot: tracking wide shot along a line of recipients receiving gifts from Harsha
panels.action: A sweeping lateral view shows Harsha moving down a long platform, giving robes to Brahmins, coins to Jain ascetics with peacock fans, and food baskets to ragged villagers waiting with anxious faces.

dialogue.text: Next come Brahmins with sacred threads, Jains with feather fans, wandering teachers of many schools, and finally the nameless poor. No single faith owns this tide of generosity.

i18n.hi: फिर आते हैं जनेऊधारी ब्राह्मण, पंखे वाले जैन, तरह-तरह के घूमते गुरु, और अंत में बेनाम ग़रीब। यह दान की बाढ़ किसी एक धर्म की नहीं।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle as attendants bring forward elephants, horses and cattle
panels.action: From a low angle, lines of elephants with decorated foreheads, restless horses and sturdy oxen are brought forward, attendants tugging their reins as Harsha gestures calmly toward groups of recipients.

dialogue.text: Not only jewels and cloth, but herds and horses pass from royal hands. Xuanzang speaks of elephants and cattle gifted away, the engines of armies and ploughs turned into offerings.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ़ गहने और कपड़े नहीं, पूरे झुंड और घोड़े भी राजहाथ से निकलते हैं। श्वेनज़ांग हाथियों और गायों के दान का ज़िक्र करता है—सेना और हल की ताकत ही भेंट बन जाती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Harsha removing his own ornaments before the crowd
panels.action: Before a dense crowd, Harsha unclaspes his necklace and armlets, handing them to attendants who carry them to waiting recipients; his face is composed, the nobles around him watchful.

dialogue.text: In the stories, he strips even his own ornaments and robe, until his sister must clothe him again. The eyewitness hints at this drama, but the heart of it is display, not ruin.

i18n.hi: किस्सों में वह अपना हार-गहना, यहाँ तक कि चोगा भी उतार देता है, और बहन को उसे फिर पहनाना पड़ता है। आँखों देखे किस्से बस इशारा करते हैं—असर दिखावे का है, बरबादी का नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up of a subordinate king kneeling and offering a casket of treasure to Harsha
panels.action: A richly dressed subordinate king kneels before Harsha, lifting up a carved casket brimming with coins and jewels, while Harsha accepts it with a measured nod before attendants carry it away.

dialogue.text: For as Harsha empties his store, the vassal rulers refill it. They offer their own treasure before the same crowd, binding their loyalty with gold, and winning honour by giving.

i18n.hi: क्योंकि जैसे ही हर्ष अपना कोश खाली करता है, आश्रित राजा उसे भर देते हैं। वही भीड़ के सामने अपना ख़ज़ाना लुटाते हैं, सोने से निष्ठा बाँधते हैं, और दान से मान कमाते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a circle of kings presenting gifts around Harsha’s raised seat
panels.action: In a ceremonial ring, lesser kings present tributes—coins, fine cloth, animals—to the attendants around Harsha’s raised seat; beyond them, the gathered communities watch with curiosity and awe.

dialogue.text: Xuanzang notes the structure plainly: the king gives on a vast scale, but the treasury is restored by those who owe him allegiance. Charity becomes an ordered exchange, not a reckless surrender.

i18n.hi: श्वेनज़ांग साफ़ लिखता है: राजा असीम देता है, पर कोश उन्हीं से भरता है जो उसके वफ़ादार हैं। दान एक सँवरा हुआ लेन-देन बन जाता है, न कि बेसिर-पैर की फ़िज़ूलखर्ची।

panels.shot: medium shot of Xuanzang-like monk observing Harsha from the crowd
panels.action: A foreign-looking monk with Chinese features stands slightly apart, hands folded, watching Harsha’s movements intently as scribes nearby scratch notes on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: The Chinese pilgrim watches all this with careful eyes—ritual bathing, distribution of wealth, offerings to stupas and shrines—and records a king who ties his name to both merit and order.

i18n.hi: चीनी यात्री यह सब तसल्ली से देखता है—स्नान, धन-वितरण, स्तूपों और देवालयों में चढ़ावे—और एक ऐसे राजा को दर्ज करता है जो अपना नाम पुण्य और नियम दोनों से बाँध देता है।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Harsha seated on the ground speaking softly to a poor family
panels.action: Harsha sits on the sand at eye-level with a thin woman and her children, handing them a bundle of grain and cloth; his guards stand discreetly back, the river glimmering beyond.

dialogue.speaker: harsha
dialogue.text: Take this, and remember only that the king has seen your hunger.

i18n.hi: इसे लो... और बस इतना याद रखो कि राजा ने तुम्हारी भूख देख ली है।

panels.shot: wide dusk shot of spent treasure mounds now empty and people dispersing
panels.action: At dusk, the once towering mounds of goods are mostly gone, the sand trampled with footprints as people drift away clutching bundles; Harsha stands quietly, silhouetted against the dim rivers.

dialogue.text: By evening, the piles of treasure have thinned. The camp smells of dust and cooking fires, of tired bodies and new possessions; the spectacle of plenty is already fading into memory.

i18n.hi: शाम तक ख़ज़ाने के ढेर पतले हो जाते हैं। डेरा धूल और पकते खाने, थके शरीर और नई चीज़ों की गंध से भरा है; यह वैभव का मंजर अभी से यादों में धुंधला होने लगा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Harsha in council tent with ministers and scribes planning the next cycle
panels.action: Harsha sits with ministers inside a lamplit tent, maps and lists spread before them, scribes writing as he gestures to routes and provinces, the faint sound of the river outside.

dialogue.text: Yet this Moksha-Dana is not a single impulse. It is one moment in a cycle—five-year rhythms of tax, tribute and gift, in which a king keeps his network stitched tight.

i18n.hi: पर यह मोक्ष-दान कोई एक जोश नहीं। यह चक्र की एक कड़ी है—पाँच-पाँच साल की कर, नज़र और दान की लय, जिससे राजा अपना जाल कसा रखता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Harsha standing alone by the river at night
panels.action: Under a sky of stars, Harsha stands alone at the river’s edge, his reflection wavering in the dark water as lanterns flicker faintly behind him in the sleeping camp.

dialogue.text: No inscription from his own court tells this scene. It survives because a foreign pilgrim wrote it down, and because the spectacle itself spoke loudly to all who saw.

i18n.hi: उसके अपने दरबार की कोई शिला-लिपि यह दृश्य नहीं बताती। यह इसलिए बचा है कि एक परदेशी यात्री ने लिख डाला, और खुद यह तमाशा देखने वालों से चीख-चीख कर बोला।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of the empty sands at Sangam at dawn after the camp has gone
panels.action: At new dawn, the vast sandbank lies almost empty, only faint impressions of poles and footprints remaining, the rivers flowing on as a lone boat crosses the misty water.

dialogue.text: Soon, the tents will vanish, the kings ride home, the poor return to their villages. But the memory of a ruler who gave and gathered at the Sangam will linger in stories and texts.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही तंबू उखड़ेंगे, राजा अपने-अपने राज्य लौटेंगे, ग़रीब अपने गाँवों को। पर संगम पर देने और बटोरने वाले इस शासक की याद कथाओं और किताबों में टँगी रहेगी।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Harsha walking away along the riverbank, attendants behind him
panels.action: Harsha walks along the riverbank, attendants following at a respectful distance, his posture straight yet unadorned, as the confluence glitters beside him in the morning sun.

dialogue.text: In Harsha’s five-year gift at Prayag, generosity is not only virtue. It is a public script in which king, faiths and people rehearse who owes what to whom—and in whose name the rivers of wealth must flow.

i18n.hi: प्रयाग में हर्ष के पंचवर्षीय दान में दया सिर्फ़ सद्गुण नहीं। यह खुला नाटक है, जिसमें राजा, धर्म और जनता बार-बार रटते हैं कि किस पर किसका हक़ है—और किसके नाम पर धन की नदियाँ बहेंगी।

subtitle_i18n.en: Harsha’s great gift at the confluence of three rivers
subtitle_i18n.hi: तीन नदियों के संगम पर हर्ष का महादान
